source_meta._title: Projectiles don't collide with the world border

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 14w17a in a new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world with cheats enabled. Use keyboard and mouse controls; where controls have been rebound, use the binding for the named action rather than the listed default key.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected snapshot Minecraft 14w17a rather than the fixed snapshot 24w33a or a newer version.
Use a separate game directory or otherwise protect existing worlds before running the old snapshot.
Create a new single-player world in Creative mode with Allow Cheats enabled so the supplied /worldborder commands can be executed.
Use Superflat terrain, or another open and level location, so blocks and terrain do not intercept the projectile before it reaches the border.
Do not install gameplay-altering mods, plugins, or datapacks.
One snowball will be used as the report's example projectile; additional projectile types are not required for the minimum reproduction.

steps.action: From the Minecraft Launcher, start the Java Edition installation configured for snapshot 14w17a and wait for the title screen to become responsive.
steps.success_cue: The title screen for Minecraft 14w17a is visible and its menu buttons respond.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, select the Superflat world type, and create the world. The Superflat choice is only a deterministic way to provide an unobstructed test area.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a newly created Creative-mode world on level, open terrain, and commands are permitted.

steps.action: Wait until the nearby terrain has rendered and normal movement and menu input respond without world-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: The terrain around the player is rendered and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Stand on an open part of the terrain with enough clear horizontal space in every direction, then remain at that position while setting the border center.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in an open area with no nearby wall or obstacle that would block a horizontally thrown snowball.

steps.action: Press T, the default Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's first command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The two relative coordinates set the border's X and Z center to the command executor's current horizontal position.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red syntax or permission error, and the world border is centered on the player's current X/Z position.

steps.action: Press T again to reopen the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready for the second command.

steps.action: Enter the report's second command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not add a transition-time argument.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red syntax or permission error and the border diameter is set to 20 blocks.

steps.action: Wait for the border to render around the player. Because its diameter is 20 blocks and it is centered on the player's former position, each flat side should be approximately 10 blocks from that center position.
steps.success_cue: A square world-border wall is visible around the test area at approximately 10 blocks from the configured center on each horizontal axis.

steps.action: Face one flat side of the world border and walk toward it while staying inside the border. Stop approximately 2 to 4 blocks before the wall, with open air between the player and the border.
steps.success_cue: One flat world-border side is directly ahead at short throwing distance, and no terrain block or entity lies between the player and that side.

steps.action: Press E, the default Inventory control, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory screen is open and shows item categories and the player's hotbar slots.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory's item-search interface, select its text field, and search for a snowball.
steps.success_cue: A Snowball item is shown among the filtered Creative inventory results.

steps.action: Pick up a stack of Snowballs from the search result and place it into an empty hotbar slot at the bottom of the inventory screen.
steps.success_cue: A Snowball stack is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Press E to close the inventory, then select the hotbar slot containing the Snowballs by pressing its corresponding number key, 1 through 9, or by scrolling to it.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed, the Snowball hotbar slot is highlighted, and a snowball is visible in the player's hand.

steps.action: Without moving outside the border, aim the crosshair horizontally and approximately perpendicular to the nearby flat border side. Keep the trajectory clear of the ground and other blocks so the projectile's first relevant intersection is with the world border.
steps.success_cue: The selected snowball is ready, the world-border wall is directly ahead, and the projected flight path is unobstructed.

steps.action: Use the selected Snowball once by pressing right-click while continuing to face the world border. Do not throw additional snowballs before handing off to observation.
steps.success_cue: One snowball has left the player's hand and is traveling directly toward the nearby world-border wall.

stor.handoff_condition: A single snowball has just been thrown from inside the 20-block-wide border directly toward an unobstructed flat side of the world border. Begin observing the snowball's interaction with the border immediately.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated-server execution, game mode, world seed, or terrain type. This plan uses a new single-player Creative Superflat world with cheats as the simplest deterministic setup that preserves the reported commands and trigger.

The report states that all projectile types are affected but explicitly offers a snowball as its example. This minimum plan tests one snowball and does not claim that Creative mode or Superflat terrain is required by the bug.

The report does not prescribe an exact throwing distance, height, or angle. The plan uses a short, approximately horizontal and perpendicular throw so terrain cannot become an alternative collision surface.
No external web verification was used because the report supplies the exact affected version, commands, border size, projectile example, and trigger action.
